facts.text: Opened in 1999 in the Mission District.
Gayle Pirie and John Clark took over the kitchen in 2001.
Named to the San Francisco Chronicle Top 100 Restaurants for twenty consecutive years.
Carmen Elias opened the Mexican bakery in 1993 after retiring from Bank of America.
Named a San Francisco legacy business in 2024.
The storefront window art is hand painted each month by a local artist.
Built in 1908 as Brown's Opera House.
Named a San Francisco Designated Landmark (no. 215) in 1996.
It is the oldest operational theatre in San Francisco.
Has a swimming pool, athletic field, playground and courts.
The Garfield Center clubhouse and pool building was renovated in 2021.
Opened in 1956 when Giovanni Giotta took over the Piccola Cafe and renamed it for Trieste.
Francis Ford Coppola wrote much of The Godfather screenplay at the cafe.
Its Saturday concert, started in 1971, is the longest running musical show in San Francisco.
facts.note: Search returned the page but only said opera singers perform on Saturdays; no 1971 start or longest-running claim.

facts.text: Opened in 1935 as Lupo's by the Cantalupo family from Naples.
Has used the same wood-burning pizza oven since 1935.
facts.note: Hoodline 2015 page returned but no result states the same oven has been used since 1935; only that a brick oven was installed in 1935.

facts.text: Awarded San Francisco Legacy Business status in 2017.
Takeout dim sum counter serving har gow, pork siu mai and baked barbecue pork buns.
Opened in 1910 as the North Beach Playground.
facts.note: Page returned; no result states a 1910 opening, only renaming in 2000 and the 2015 renovation.

facts.text: Vince, Joe and Dom DiMaggio grew up playing baseball here in the 1920s.
facts.note: No result mentions Vince, Dom or 1920s; only that Joe DiMaggio played at North Beach and other parks.

facts.text: A renovation was completed in November 2015.
Vincent Correnti opened it in 1984; three generations of his family have owned it.
Joined the San Francisco Legacy Business Registry on May 23, 2022.
Temple to the god Guan Di, relocated to the Kong Chow Building in 1977.
The original Pine Street temple was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake and fire.
Named a Bib Gourmand by the MICHELIN Guide.
facts.note: Michelin page lists Rooh as a MICHELIN restaurant ($$$) but no result shows a Bib Gourmand designation.

facts.text: Serves modern Indian cuisine made with fresh California produce.
facts.note: Michelin snippet says modern Indian fusing flavors with oysters, pork belly, burrata; no mention of California produce.

facts.text: Established in 2008 on the Embarcadero waterfront.
Chef Parke Ulrich leads the kitchen.
Has served sandwiches at 8th and Harrison since 1993.
Written up in SF Weekly's Cheap Eats and the Chronicle's Bargain Bites.
Listed in the MICHELIN Guide for Japanese and Californian cuisine.
Founded by two Four Barrel Coffee partners and a former Tartine pastry chef.
Is a Jewish diaspora bakery that announced a second location.
Designated San Francisco Landmark #264.
First opened in 1935 and became a gay bar with open plate glass windows in 1972.
facts.note: Wikipedia: opened 1935; oversized windows unveiled 1972 (one snippet says window coverings removed a year later).

facts.text: Chef Melissa Perello's restaurant won a Michelin star.
Reopened in June 2021 after a pandemic closure.
facts.note: SFGate says Frances reopened Thursday June 23 with a prix-fixe format (Hoodline 2022/06 matches), i.e. 2022, not June 2021.

facts.text: Opened in 1995 by Michael and Mary Gassen as a full-line neighborhood artisan bakery.
Named to the San Francisco Chronicle's Top 100 Bay Area Restaurants in 2018.
Founders Massimiliano Conti and Lorella Degan sold it to a restaurant group.
Has a multi-level back patio with picnic tables.
